mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate level is inversely related to equity returns. A lower FEDFUNDS level consistently leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is always active, and the direction is fixed to '+' because the relationship is negative: lower rates imply positive returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below 4.5% (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 300 signals persistent inflation, which may lead to aggressive monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal activates when CPIAUCSL exceeds 300.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 300, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals a tightening monetary policy combined with high inflation, which increases the risk of recession and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal activates when both series are rising (3-month change positive).
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL have positive 3-month changes (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A housing market weakness, defined by housing starts (HOUST) below 1300 and residential investment (RSAFS) below 700,000, signals a demand shock in the housing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal activates only in this regime.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST < 1300 AND RSAFS < 700000, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The unemployment rate (UNRATE) is inversely related to equity returns. A lower UNRATE level consistently leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is always active, and the direction is fixed to '+' because the relationship is negative: lower unemployment implies positive returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE is below 4% (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) below 1300 signal weak demand in the housing sector, which may lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. The signal activates when HOUST falls below 1300.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST < 1300, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and fall in housing starts (HOUST) signals a supply shock in manufacturing combined with weak housing demand, which increases the risk of recession and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. The signal activates when INDPRO has a positive 3-month change and HOUST has a negative 3-month change.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO has a positive 3-month change and HOUST has a negative 3-month change (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) below 102.5 signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which may lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal activates when INDPRO falls below 102.5.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 102.5, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
